reason: Tier 2: add a gated last-item residual inside the existing GRU representation. Recurrence improved macro HR@10 from 0.5050 to 0.5737, while 32-to-8 hard-negative mining reached only 0.5700; this suggests testing the representation rather than further increasing negative difficulty. A plausible bottleneck is that recurrent compression loses immediate item identity, particularly for short purchase transitions, although the available results do not establish this cause.

plan.model_design: Add a jointly trained, feature-wise gated residual from each current input-item embedding to its GRU output before the existing projection and normalization. In GRURec.encode, retain the undropped input_norm(self.embedding(seq)) tensor as local_features, compute recurrent_features with the existing dropout and GRU, and form fused_features = recurrent_features + sigmoid(gate(concat(recurrent_features, local_features))) * local_features before applying the existing projection. This gives next-item prediction direct access to immediate item identity while retaining the recurrent representation of earlier purchases; initialize gate weights to zero and its bias to -2 so training begins near the existing architecture. Preserve GRURec.__init__, encode, score, and predict signatures, existing attributes, normalized tied embeddings, bias, log_scale, and one jointly optimized network per category; do not introduce separate prediction heads or combine independent scores.
